episodes.177683: A lightning strike caused some damage to a home.
episodes.177949: Unseasonably warm temperatures occurred in the first two weeks of April, with highs near 80 degrees occurring at times. These warm temps, along with occasional rain, resulted in melting of a deep snowpack on top of frozen ground which led to significant runoff into area waterways. Moderate to major flooding occurred along portions of the Milk River and its tributaries. Impactful snowmelt flooding also occurred across Southcentral Montana, in particular across the Gallatin Valley.
episodes.178456: Unsettled weather with numerous showers and thunderstorms were observed due to an upper level cut-off low strengthening northwest of Puerto Rico. Strong divergence aloft resulted in hail, and the heavy rain left flooding, mudslides and rivers overflowing.
episodes.179185: Showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front moving in from the northwest developed over the Eastern Shore of Maryland, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.179683: A slow, strong storm moved across Calcasieu Lake during the evening of the 6th. Strong wind gusts were recorded around the lake.
episodes.179684: A strong and slow moving thunderstorm south of Lake Charles produced 10 to 20 inches of rain during the evening.
episodes.179722: A strong cold front resulted in the development of slow-moving thunderstorms with very heavy rain across portions of the Triangle. This resulted in multiple road and highway closures, particularly around Fuquay-Varina.
episodes.179850: Flooding occurred in portions of Montgomery and Austin Counties as storms moved through the area during the night of April 6 and morning of April 7.
episodes.179936: A stalled frontal boundary was in place for a couple days across the region. This feature was the focal point for numerous showers and thunderstorms. Weak mid level flow aided in slow movement of storms that did develop. One of those stronger slow moving storms produced flash flooding around Baton Rouge and hail in Galliano.
episodes.180117: Thunderstorms moved across Upstate South Carolina during the morning in association with a cold front. One storm producing intense lightning caused a minor injury in Gaffney.

events.narrative: Wires down at intersection of Blue Jay Lane and Canterbury Road. Time estimated via radar.
A wind gust of 56 mph was recorded at Hebert's Marina.
High water was reported in the Dobbin area due to heavy rain around the intersection of Dobbin Rd and FM1486.

Numerous roadways were flooded and impassable in Hackberry and Grand Lake. A maximum rainfall amount reported was just over 19 inches in Hackberry with around 1 foot common in Grand Lake. The majority of the rain occurred during 3 hours. Three homes had minor flooding during the event in Grand Lake.
Numerous roads were flooded near the Calcasieu-Cameron Parish line. A high water rescue was conducted near the intersection of Helms and Tom Hebert Roads when a car became stranded.
Lighting caused a house fire on Knoboak Drive near the intersection of Hammerly Blvd and Gessner Road.
During a thunderstorm, winds were sustained at 20 to 30 knots and gusting to 25 to 36 knots for 1 hour between 8:30 and 9:30 LST. Winds reached a peak gust of 36 knots at Cameron.
Roads north of Lothair become flooded from snowmelt. Liberty Co law enforcement closed several sections of several roads across the county.
A house fire was reported due to a lightning strike, which burned the attic.
A roadway was closed near the intersection of North Carolina Highway 55 and North Carolina Highway 42.
A flooded roadway was reported near Brookside Drive in Fuquay-Varina.
A road closure was reported near the intersection of Holland Road and Mayfair Wood Road.
Both lanes of FM 2429 between SH 36 and GM 949 were closed due to floodwaters making the road impassable.
High water reported on Scenic Highway on the north side of Baton Rouge.
